paragraphs.text:
Boss: Good morning! How are you today?

Account Manager: I’m fine, thank you. How about you?

Boss: I’m good, thanks. Let’s talk about your work with Tork this month.

Account Manager: Sure! I visited five clients last week. They are happy with the products.

Boss: That’s great to hear! Did you introduce the new Tork hand towels?

Account Manager: Yes, I did. Three clients placed orders for the new hand towels.

Boss: Excellent! What about the others?

Account Manager: They need more time to decide. One client asked for a sample.

Boss: Good. Make sure they get the sample this week.

Account Manager: I will.

Boss: And how are the sales targets for this month?

Account Manager: We are at 70% of the target.

Boss: That’s not bad, but we need to reach 100%. Can you follow up with more clients?

Account Manager: Yes, I will call them today and tomorrow.

Boss: Perfect. Let me know if you need help.

Account Manager: Thank you, Mr. Brown.

Boss: Keep up the good work!

Account Manager: I will. Thank you!

questions.question: How many clients did the account manager visit last week?
What product did the account manager introduce?
choices: B. A sample of hand soap

questions.question: How many clients placed orders for the new product?
What percentage of the sales target has the team reached?
What did the boss tell the account manager to do about clients who need more time?
choices: B. Follow up and give them samples

Anna: Hi, I’m Anna. I just joined the company last week. It’s nice to meet you!

James: Hi Anna, I’m James. Welcome to the team! How are you finding it so far?

Anna: Everyone has been very kind. I’m still getting to know the work, but it’s been good. How long have you been here?

James: About three years now. It’s a great place to work. So, do you have any children?

Anna: Yes, I do! I have two daughters. Lily is 10, and Emma is 7. What about you?

James: I have one son, Alex. He’s 8. Does Lily like school?

Anna: She loves it, especially art and music. Emma is more into sports. What about Alex?

James: He’s very active, too. He loves football, and he’s starting to learn how to play the piano. What do your daughters look like?

Anna: Lily is tall and has straight brown hair. Emma is shorter and has curly blond hair. And Alex?

James: He has short dark hair and big brown eyes. He’s very curious about everything. It’s fun to watch him learn new things!

B. He has straight brown hair.
C. He has short dark hair and big brown eyes.
D. He has curly blond hair.

paragraphs.text:
Sarah: Hi, I’m Sarah. Is your child playing today?

Mark: Yes! My son, Jake, is number 10. He plays as a striker. What about yours?

Sarah: My daughter, Emily, is number 5. She’s a defender. It’s her first season playing.

Mark: That’s great! Jake loves scoring goals, but defenders are so important to the team.

Sarah: Yes, Emily is learning how to tackle and pass better. The coach says she’s improving.

Mark: The referee is blowing the whistle… Oh no, a penalty for the other team!

Sarah: That looked like a soft foul to me. But let’s see if our goalkeeper can save it.

Mark: Fingers crossed! So, does Emily enjoy playing?

Sarah: She loves it! She’s made so many friends on the team. How about Jake?

Mark: He’s always been crazy about football. He even watches matches every weekend!

Sarah: That’s dedication! Oh, look—Emily just made a great tackle!

Mark: Nice one! This is turning into a really exciting match.

B. The referee stopped the game
